title: False Teachers and False Prophets
lead: From Moses to the last letters of the New Testament, the Bible warns about people who speak in God's name but lead his people astray, and gives tests for telling them apart. The prophets' tests are laid out on "The False Prophet."

sections.h: Tests in the Law and the Prophets
sections.b: A prophet whose sign comes true but who says "Let us follow other gods" is a false prophet (Deuteronomy 13:1–5), and so is one whose word does not come true (Deuteronomy 18:20–22). Jeremiah attacks prophets who say "Peace, peace" when there is no peace and who tell their own dreams (Jeremiah 6:14; 23:16–32). Ezekiel says false visions will end, calls prophets who cover a weak wall with whitewash false, and says a prophet who is deceived shares the guilt of the one who asked him (Ezekiel 12:24; 13:1–23; 14:9–10); he also condemns shepherds who feed themselves (Ezekiel 34).
sections.refs: Deuteronomy 13:1–5; Deuteronomy 18:20–22; Jeremiah 6:14; Jeremiah 23:16–32; Ezekiel 13; Ezekiel 34:1–10; Ezekiel 12:24; Ezekiel 14:9–10

sections.b: Jesus warns of false prophets "in sheep's clothing" and gives the test of fruit (Matthew 7:15–20), and predicts many false messiahs (Matthew 24:11, 24). Paul warns the Ephesian elders of "savage wolves" (Acts 20:29–30). The later letters, 2 Peter 2, 1 John 4:1–3 and Jude, deal with such teachers already inside the churches. Revelation uses "the false prophet" for one figure of the end; see that topic.
sections.refs: Matthew 7:15–20; Matthew 24:11; Matthew 24:24; Acts 20:29–30; 2 Corinthians 11:13–15; 2 Peter 2:1–3; 1 John 4:1–3
